name: Replit Agent
operator: Replit (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Replit's own public documentation, product, security, subprocessor and customer pages, and its published llms.txt
what: Replit's AI agent that builds, runs, tests and publishes software from a description in plain language, inside a Replit project.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: two assessors working blind, a challenger, then the scorer.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: This carries Autonomy 3 and 4, so I argued against it. What the page (read 2026-11-10) says: the title says "Production SLA Dashboard"; the build was at a hackathon ("2 hour build-a-thon"); it is "Currently serving as an internal dashboard"; the saving is Natalie Mercuri's estimate ("could reduce"); extending it to customers is described as what could happen. Only the page heading names Agent ("with Replit Agent"); the body says "Replit". Two things follow. (1) The capability that acts here is Agent building software, and the thing in use is the dashboard it built; the scope asks for a customer or usage figures "for the capability that acts", and a hackathon prototype in internal use is closer to "a demonstration" than to routine production work. (2) A3 is described as completing routine tasks end to end in production; one vendor-published story is the only support. The span is exact and the grade documented is right, and the note already says the savings are the story's estimates. Decision for the studio and Dinis: either keep S1 and say plainly on the card that it is one internal prototype, or find a second source (a usage figure for Agent, a customer in production). Without S1 the scorer gives A2, not A4.

A4 needs I10 and I10 is available, not default (connectors the user adds; the "As shipped" configuration says no external connectors). The source and span are right ("Read and write to external services like BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion"). The issue is how the card reads: with S1, A4 holds only with connectors on; as shipped it is A3. The card should say which configuration its level holds in. See also request to gamma-ray@.

The second load-bearing fact for A3 and A4. The span "Chat with Agent to refine your project, then publish when you're ready." is exact, but it is a how-to step, not a statement that Agent works independently and the person approves critical decisions only. I searched the overview and the other cited Agent pages and found no sentence that says Agent works on its own by default. The nearest is on the App Testing page: "Extended Autonomy ... work for longer periods without requiring human intervention", which is I17 and available only with App Testing on (Power or Max mode). The note also folds Plan mode ("the person approves the plan") into a default answer; Plan mode is a configuration (I07 is tied to plan-mode). Cite a sentence that states the independence, or mark I18 as holding only with App Testing.

Span "the Agent will pop up with a button to" (9 words) is exact on the App Testing page, as is the Power or Max requirement. It is the source for independence that I18 lacks; consider whether I18 should lean on it.

Exact and correctly available: "By default, background tasks wait for you to review and apply their changes. You can enable Automatically apply changes". Note that this default is the opposite of I19, so it is a good example of a fact that raises Autonomy only when the person turns it on.

Span is exact. Credit holds as a default, but note it is about changes by background tasks held for review, not about a gate on all high-impact actions (publishing, connectors). It carries Control 1 and 2 with I25.
Exact and correctly available (Enterprise only). It is the second fact of Control 2 (I38 and I23 or I25), so Control 2 holds only on Enterprise. Same remark as I10 on how the card shows it.

"An internal security harness continuously probes and tests the AI Agent" is the vendor's own statement and is credited as such. The indicator needs the operation, so documented does not count. Honest as written.
The note says the external testing covers the platform and does not name Agent. That is what the page says (HackerOne bug bounty, Trail of Bits). Correct and careful.

The subprocessors page names Anthropic and OpenAI as AI models and Google as cloud infrastructure and AI models. It lists providers, not which model Agent uses; the help page says the model behind Agent "can't be swapped". The credit as "models and third-party components listed" is fair; the note could say it is a list of providers.
Not credited, and the not_credited entry says why (SOC 2 stated, no report). Correct: Openness 4 is not claimed.

Eight spans differ from the source only in the apostrophe (the pages use a curly one, the scan a straight one: I01, I07, I18, I21, I38, I47, I57, S2). The words are exact. If the gate or a reader compares character by character, normalise one way.

Opened each source. The note says what the page says; the grade documented is right (S3 observed: llms.txt resolves and lists Agent, MCP, security pages); mode is right (I07 plan-mode, I11 connectors, I47 custom instructions are available; the rest are default). Spans are under fifteen words (the longest, I21, has 14). I39: "Select Stop in the Agent panel to halt it immediately" is on the help page. I68: the changelog index lists a dated entry for 6 November 2026. I22: freezing, looping and unrequested features are on the help page.

Round one answered; re-read. The new source is a Forbes article reposted on Replit's newsroom (the funding announcement). The span "Zillow has roughly 600 Replit seats for its employees" is exact (8 words), and the page goes on: "who have made more than 7,000 apps using the tool over the past year" and that customers "use it to build internal apps for their teams". Against it: (1) the figures are seats of the platform and a count of apps, not usage of Agent; the article says "Replit" and "the tool", and calls the product "an AI agent that could write its own code" only in its origin story, and it announces Agent 4 as new. (2) The reader cannot see the article's date in the page text. (3) It is a vendor-hosted reprint, and its only voice for Zillow is a quote about prototyping. For it: it names a customer and gives a usage figure over a year, in internal use, which is more than a hackathon. My verdict: S1 stands as a named customer with usage figures (the literal test), and it is stronger than Plaid. It is not evidence that the agent "completes routine tasks end to end" for anyone; the card should not word Autonomy 3 as if it were. I do not block it. The Plaid story, kept as second source in the note, is fine as written.

New span "Agent handles the rest, from planning to deployment" is exact (overview). It is a sentence of the vendor's description of the product, not a measurement; credit as documented is correct. Two small points: the note also says "paid actions need confirmation", which is from the Agent modes page, not the overview the answer cites, and it is a statement about cost, not a critical decision of the work; and "changes from background tasks wait for the person's review" is from the task lifecycle page. The facts are true and on those pages; either cite them or drop them from the note so the source and the note match. Plan toggle off: "Agent builds directly" is on the plan mode page, which confirms the default.

Argued against Autonomy 4 as a whole. A4 is "Runs multi-step workflows across systems or coordinates other agents". Replit reaches it by S1 (A3), I10 and I19 or I18. I10 is a list of connectors Agent can read and write ("BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion"), available when the person adds them. Nothing on the cited pages says Agent runs a multi-step workflow across them; the page says Agent "can read and write data directly". The rule gives A4 to any agent that reaches A3 and has connectors, so the card says A4 for what the sources show only as a capability. Round one: the studio agreed as shipped it reads A3. Condition for approval: the card must show the configuration that A4 holds in (connectors on) and that A3 rests on S1 above. I have already asked gamma-ray@; this is not for the studio to fix in the scan.
Exact and available. It satisfies "I18 or I19" for A4 together with I18, so A4 does not rest on it alone.
C2 (I38 and I23 or I25) holds only on Enterprise through I25. The card should say so. Not a level three or four.

Levels three and four on the card: only Autonomy 4. No level three or four on Reach (2), Control (2), Openness (0). The levels argued above. Round-one findings: S1 changed and re-sourced, I18 re-sourced, I61 and the apostrophes done; I10, I25 and the other notes were agreed with no change needed, which I accept.

responses.response: Changed. S1 now cites the Forbes article on Replit's newsroom: Zillow, about 600 seats, more than 7,000 apps over a year, a named customer with usage figures over a year rather than one hackathon. It says 'Replit', and the same article describes the product as an AI agent writing its own code; the Plaid story, which names Replit Agent, is kept in the note as a second source. Whether a customer's apps built by the agent meet S1's 'capability that acts' is the scope question you put to gamma-ray@; we read it as yes, because building and deploying the app is what the agent does on its own.

Changed. Span now 'Agent handles the rest, from planning to deployment' (overview); the plan-mode page also says that with the Plan toggle off Agent builds directly, which is the default. Plan mode is no longer folded into the note.

Agreed: A4 holds only with connectors on; as shipped the card reads A3 (with S1). The card marks I10 as available; showing the level per configuration is the card's layout, asked of gamma-ray@ in your request. No change to the answer.
Agreed, Control 2 holds on Enterprise only; same as I10. No change to the answer.
Changed: the note says it is a list of providers, not of the model Agent uses.
Changed: the spans of I01, I07, I21, I38, I47, I57 and S2 now use the page's curly apostrophe. I18 has a new span.
Note trimmed to what the cited overview says; the paid-action confirmation (another page) is no longer in it.

not_credited.what: Replit states a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation.
not_credited.why: No report or scope statement is public, and nothing says it covers Agent rather than the company; the trust centre's content did not load without JavaScript. Not counted as an independent check yet.

not_credited.what: The main chat hands tasks to parallel worker chats that report back.
not_credited.why: One agent delegating sub-tasks for the same person and project; the indicator for several agents coordinating asks for more.

not_credited.what: An MCP scanner blocks suspicious tools before they run.
not_credited.why: A gate before a tool runs, not detection of anomalies in operation.
